title: Me-MPK: Accelerating Krylov Subspace Solvers via Memory-efficient Matrix-Power Kernel
problem: Matrix-Power Kernels (MPK) for Krylov subspace methods rely on repeated SpMVs with the same matrix but suffer from data dependencies that block cache reuse and symmetric SpMVs incur data conflicts during shared-memory parallelization, limiting speedup on multi-core CPUs.
motivation: Large sparse linear systems in circuit simulation, HPC, and scientific computing require efficient Krylov solvers; existing methods optimize matrix reuse OR symmetry independently, missing the opportunity to exploit both simultaneously.
method: Me-MPK constructs a unified dependency graph for sparse matrices capturing all potential dependencies and conflicts; performs architecture-aware recursive partitioning into independent subgraphs with a separating subgraph that decouples conflicts; schedules subgraphs for parallel SpMV/symmetric-SpMV execution in order to maximize cache reuse while eliminating synchronization overhead.
key_novelty: Unified dependency graph approach enabling simultaneous exploitation of matrix reuse and symmetry, paired with recursive partitioning to create conflict-free independent subgraphs for ordered parallel execution.
contributions: Unified dependency graph model capturing cache reuse and symmetry conflict information
Architecture-aware recursive partitioning algorithm for conflict decoupling
Ordered parallel execution strategy optimizing cache reuse across subgraphs
1.65× and 1.58× overall solver speedup on X86 and ARM respectively (2.0× and 1.86× on MPK kernel alone)
baselines: prior matrix-reuse and symmetry-aware SpMV approaches
limitations: Overhead of partitioning and conflict detection not characterized; scalability to GPU/heterogeneous architectures not addressed.
primary_theme: memory-efficient sparse solver via unified dependency-driven partitioning
